Table~\ref{tab:lit-term-check} sorts the terms by a comparison made after the
search. A term counts as listed when it, with its truncation, is an entry of a
published term list or a phrase within an entry. The lists are those reported by
works cited in this thesis: Baumann et
al.~\parencite[App.~A, Table~6]{baumann2025llm}, Hutton et
al.~\parencite[Table~2]{hutton2018assessing}, Malki et
al.~\parencite[Sec.~3.1]{malki2024exploring}, Salehzadeh Niksirat et
al.~\parencite[Sec.~1.2]{niksirat2024wearable} and Shipp and
Blasco~\parencite[Sec.~3.1]{shipp2020period} searched apps or literature with
theirs, and Doan et al.~\parencite[Sec.~4.5]{doan2024transparency} searched policy
text. Any other term is checked against the titles and abstracts of the 128 works
held before the search, 45 of which have no abstract in the records; these are the
works that entered through the citations of the thesis or the Methods Digest. A spelling or
inflection of another term takes that term's result.

\section{Search Strings}
\label{app:lit-strings}
The strings below were sent to each platform on 28 October 2026 (times in
UTC). No language or publication-type filter was set; both are screening rules.
Each anchor query pairs one domain word with one privacy term, or joins the words
of one privacy-text term, in the title or abstract. Bracketed numbers after the
arXiv anchor queries are the records each returned. The strands applied locally to the arXiv pool, the ACL Anthology file
and the venue lists use the term groups of Table~\ref{tab:lit-groups-full} and the
rules of Table~\ref{tab:lit-strands}, with the matching rules of
\texttt{lit.py}: text and terms are reduced to lower-case letters and digits, a
trailing * matches any word ending, and terms match only whole words. The PACM~HCI issues that carry CSCW papers are named
\enquote{CSCW} until 2024; from 2025 the issues are numbered, so all its 2025
and 2026 issues were listed. The search results are kept unchanged in
\texttt{05\_Data/Literature Search/28. Oct/}.
